notes.title: Discovering the roots of Depths of Ascension's world - Devlog 05
notes.content:
If you've ever wondered how such a rich era of history and mythology like ancient Mesopotamia and Sumeria can influence the world of gaming, then you're in the right place!

In this [b]devlog[/b], we'll get to know more of [b]Depths of Ascension[/b] and explore how these ancient civilizations have inspired both the visual and narrative aspects of the game.

     To begin with, it's important to understand the cultural and historical significance of these ancient civilizations. Mesopotamia, often referred to as the “Cradle of Civilization”, was home to some of the world's earliest cities and empires. And within this fertile land, the Sumerian civilization flourished, known for its advanced cuneiform writing, complex legal and religious systems, and epic legends such as that of Gilgamesh.

     The art of these civilizations wasn’t only aesthetically impressive but also a profound expression of their religious and mythological beliefs. From relief sculptures depicting gods to palace reliefs telling stories of real battles and triumphs, Mesopotamian art offers us an incredible insight into their worldviews and values.

     When we began conceiving the art style for the game, we wanted to capture the authenticity and atmosphere of these ancient civilizations. From the details of the clothing to the mysterious symbols engraved on monuments, every visual element was carefully crafted to transport players to an immersive and richly detailed world.

     In addition to the art, the game's narrative concept is also inspired by Sumerian narratives. Yehpa's journey in search of her lost sister echoes Ishtar's descent into the underworld in Mesopotamian mythology. Just as Ishtar descends into the dark realms in search of her sister, but also driven by the ambition to acquire knowledge and renewal, Yehpa ventures into unknown and dangerous lands in search of her sister, facing challenges and trials along the way.

     The narrative of [b]Depths of Ascension[/b] resonates with themes of sacrifice, self-knowledge, and spiritual rebirth present in Ishtar's story, offering players an exciting and meaningful journey.

[b]It is crucial to highlight that Kishar is not limited to being just a fantasy representation of Mesopotamia, but rather a world of its own, full of unique characteristics and peculiarities, where Mesopotamian culture serves as a fundamental inspiration, intertwined with elements of fantasy.[/b]

Add [b]Depths of Ascension[/b] to your [b]Wishlist[/b] now and get ready to witness this adventure!

notes.title: The Ka'tar People: Parasitic Fungi and Their Complex Society - Devlog 04
notes.content:
Today, let's dive into the culture of the Ka'tar People. Although they may initially appear as antagonists, it's important to understand that their biological and cultural characteristics put them in a position of conflict with other humanoid races.

[i]Meaning of the name (in Sumerian): ka-tar    princely; praise; challenger; a type of fungus or rot ('mouth' + 'to decide; to destroy')
[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904748/41b498400c27ef353e3aaca9ab885c9e41800e40.png[/img]

The Ka'tar are parasitic fungi that depend on infecting the brain of a humanoid host to survive and reproduce. This dependency puts them in a conflicted relationship with their hosts, as their very existence requires our subjugation. This inevitable imbalance is one of the reasons why the Ka'tar are seen as a threat by humanoid peoples.

Furthermore, the Ka'tar lack a full understanding of human notions, resulting in behaviors often incomprehensible to others. The emotions they express on their faces are remnants of the host they infected, not their own, creating an additional layer of strangeness and incomprehension. While they require vital parts of the body to sustain themselves, other parts decay due to their influence. For example, the Ka'tar relies on the host's eyes for sight and their digestive system for sustenance, so those parts of the body are preserved while others decompose.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904748/e339fad7a63b7702afd92b270e20dea7d0297cef.png[/img]

Inhabitants of the Ancient Temple of Ashni for a decade now, the Ka'tar demonstrate an ability to adapt to diverse environments and explore spaces, living in colonies that reflect not only collective dependence but also the ability to organize and coordinate in relation to hosts.

[b]Imagine encountering someone you know transformed by a parasitic entity?
[/b]
In [b]Depths of Ascension[/b], we will explore these nuances further, challenging players to face not only physical enemies but also ethical and emotional dilemmas.

We are excited to [b]share[/b] more details about the [b]game's development[/b] and can't wait to see players dive into the depths of this journey!

Keep following our [b]devlogs[/b] and our [b]social media[/b] channels for more updates and insights on the development of [b]Depths of Ascension[/b]!

notes.title: 2D vs 3D and Unity vs Unreal - Devlog 03
notes.content:
The initial plan for [b]Depths of Ascension[/b] was to develop it in [b]Unity[/b], completely in 2D. However, a turnaround occurred when Unity's monetization policy changed, introducing an installation fee. It wasn't just the fee itself that made us reconsider the engine choice, but the unpredictability associated with future contractual changes. The sense that [b]Unity[/b] could retroactively modify contracts, as they attempted the previous year, made us rethink our decision.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904748/44b73ba0942b79ac7c20ed6b407c0a3e8a4303d7.png[/img]

Development was scheduled to begin on November 5th, a commitment established with the management of the grant that funded the production of this vertical slice. We had a short time to decide which engine to use and learn how to use it. We opted for [b]Unreal [/b]due to its visual capabilities and decided to adapt the project to 2.5D, with 2D characters in a 3D environment.

As we explored the transition to a 3D environment with 2D sprites, we faced significant challenges with shadows. Initially, we tried to have 3D walls and 2D sprites, but the sprites, positioned at a 45° angle to the camera, caused clipping through the walls.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904748/3be55ef13afc25c1421edd6afd5438cac9ea0e6c.png[/img]

To work around this, we decided to turn the walls into 2D sprites, aligning them with the characters. This solved the clipping issue of the walls but introduced a new obstacle: the 2D sprites continued to cause clipping on the 3D floor. Despite attempts, we didn't find a viable solution to render the 2D sprites above the 3D elements properly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904748/0359583f6599012226f4d6983a1ffe77abe58c15.png[/img]

Faced with this impasse, we considered making the game entirely in 3D. However, this option was initially discarded due to the lack of a 3D artist on the team. Fortunately, we were able to hire a 3D artist, which allowed us to revisit this decision. We then decided to migrate the project entirely to 3D, believing that this would solve the shadow and clipping challenges we were facing.

This change represented a significant milestone in the development of [b]Depths of Ascension[/b], and we hope it will allow us to progress more smoothly and effectively in the future!

Our [b]devlogs[/b] are a window into the creation process, where we share our experiences, learnings, and progress. Follow us on [url=https://www.instagram.com/prometheaninteractive/][b]Instagram[/b][/url] to learn more about the challenges we face and the creative solutions we find as we develop our game!

notes.title: Tackling Turn-Based Strategies - Devlog 02
notes.content:
Greetings, summoner!

​It is with great enthusiasm that we bring another devlog of our game in development, [b]Depths of Ascension[/b]. In this devlog, we will explore in detail the intricate turn-based system and general resources that underpin the gameplay of our game.

At the heart of [b]DoA[/b] lies a robust and dynamic turn-based system designed to offer an immersive and strategic experience to players.

[b]Tick - Game Time Unit[/b]:

Every action, every movement, is governed by the fundamental unit of time in the game, known as the “tick”.

[b]Actor[/b]:

In [b]DoA[/b], each entity, whether the protagonist of the demo Yehpa, the enemies faced, or the challenging elements of the environment, is considered an actor. Each of them has the ability to perform actions that shape the course of the adventure.

[b]Action Bar (AB)[/b]:

The action bar is the measure of the time remaining for an actor to perform its action. It decreases according to the actor's speed, and when it reaches 0, the action is triggered, moving the narrative forward.

[b]Speed and Action Cost[/b]:

Speed ​​determines how quickly an actor's AB depletes with each tick. Each action, in turn, has an associated cost, adding a crucial strategic element to players' choices.

[b]Early Action and Delayed Action[/b]:

Actions in [b]DoA[/b] are distinct in their temporal effects. While early actions have their effects immediately triggered after the choice, delayed actions wait for the depletion of the AB.

[b]Tick and Action Structure[/b]:

With every game tick, the AB of all actors is reduced, moving the game forward. When an actor's AB reaches 0, its delayed action is executed, triggering a series of events and reactions that shape the narrative.

[b]Player's Turn[/b]:

Players take control during the player's turn. When the player's AB reaches 0, the tick count stops, and the player can choose their next action, allowing players to decide the next step of their journey.

[b]Action Tags[/b]:

Actions in [b]DoA[/b] are categorized by tags that influence other aspects of the game. From physical actions that consume Stamina, which each character has a maximum value determined by their constitution and strength, to those that require the expenditure of Mana, tags add depth and complexity to players' choices.

Now, delving into the details of the [b]resources[/b] and [b]magic[/b] that shape and deepen the world of [b]Depths of Ascension[/b], let's explore how these elements shape the player's experience and influence the strategies adopted during the journey.

[b]Satiety[/b]:

An essential resource that reflects the need for food and survival. The speed at which satiety decreases depends on the character's constitution, while recovery occurs through eating. NPCs, on the other hand, are exempt from this concern. When the character is satiated, the regeneration value of Stamina and Health Points of the character increases by 20%. When hungry, the character's Stamina regeneration value decreases by 10%, and gradually decreases according to their level of hunger.

[b]Health Points (HP)[/b]:

HP represents the characters' life and is affected by damage received. HP regeneration is determined by the character's constitution, while their regeneration speed is defined by their race. When HP reaches 0, the character dies.

[b]Magical Resources[/b]:

The world of [b]DoA[/b] is permeated by magical energies, each with its unique characteristics, but only one will be implemented in the demo:

         [b]Divine Magic[/b]: Granted by the deities, it is practiced by priests like Yehpa - the main character of the demo. The use of Divine Actions consumes Favour Points, which are recovered through prayer.

The turn-based system of [b]DoA[/b] is much more than a game mechanic; it is a tool for storytelling, challenging players, and creating unique experiences with each session. Resources and spells are fundamental elements that enrich the player's experience and add depth to the game universe. From managing satiety and Stamina to the strategic use of resources and magic, players will be challenged to explore and master these aspects on their journey to ascension.

[b]We are excited to share more details about the game's development and can't wait to see players dive into the depths of this journey!

Keep following our devlogs and our social media channels for more updates and insights on the development of Depths of Ascension![/b]

notes.title: Explore, Do Stuff, and then Explore Some More - Devlog 01
notes.content:
Exploration is the core of [b]roguelike[/b] games! From unpredictable maps to cunning enemies, every step is an invitation to enchantment and constant discovery. We challenge players to enhance their adaptive skills in the face of uncertainty, providing a rewarding experience of wonder as they unravel intriguing secrets and challenges. Exploration is not just crucial; it is the fuel that keeps the flame of progress alive!

Truly fascinating, [b]roguelikes[/b] transform the game with procedural generation, immersing players in ever-changing environments where unpredictability is the norm. Each maze and scenario is procedurally built, ensuring that each run is unique. This feature not only maintains constant wonder but also redefines permadeath as an opportunity, promising a new world with every foray into the genre's universe.

Our first [b]build[/b] is entirely focused on exploration, establishing the foundation for an engaging experience. In testing this phase, we chose to highlight the essence of the player's initial interaction with the virtual world, setting aside more complex mechanics. [b]Our goal?[/b] To ensure that simply exploring is a fun and engaging experience. We worked on the fluidity of movements, visually captivating landscapes, and surprises during exploration, creating the groundwork for future additions of mechanics that enhance, but do not replace, the joy of traversing an intriguing virtual world.

The [b]demo[/b] area, will be an isolated testing ground, carefully separated from the main dungeon of the final game. This approach aims to offer players an exclusive and controlled preview, exploring a tantalizing fragment of the game's universe. By isolating this test area, our development team can focus on presenting the initial mechanics, narrative, and atmosphere, ensuring a cohesive and impactful initial experience. This strategic separation allows specific adjustments to the demo, fine-tuning difficulties and offering an engaging glimpse of the game's proposal without revealing all its secrets. We can't wait to share!

In [b]Depths of Ascension[/b], lighting plays a crucial role, as it takes place underground where natural light is scarce. Light sources such as fluorescent fungi, torches, and magic are crucial for navigation, making the search for illumination and the possibility of being in the dark essential elements in gameplay. All playable races rely on vision as their primary means of perceiving the environment, exploring NPC perception, with monsters attracted to light. The strategy extends beyond vision, encompassing senses like smell, hearing, and magic perception, providing crucial information to face enemies and challenges. Even in blindness, players can navigate through sound and smells, highlighting the importance of sensory exploration.

[b]Depths of Ascension[/b] is an engaging fusion of exploration, procedural generation, and gameplay enhancement, fueled by meticulous attention to atmosphere. From the unpredictable challenges of [b]roguelikes[/b] to the delicate choreography between light and darkness, each element contributes to building captivating and memorable digital worlds.

We invite you to embark on this journey with us!

Follow us on social media for exclusive behind-the-scenes glimpses, exciting updates, and share your passion for the unique intersection of art, technology, and entertainment!
